To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chickens containing B22 had a higher survival rate than those not containing B22.
the B26 haplotype is a major gene for resistance to RSV-induced sarcomas in the chicken and that the B22 haplo-type is a second, minor gene for resistance.
chickens containing the B22 haplo-type are more resistant to Rous sarcomea virus-induced tumors than those containing B26 and B 30.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic control of the immune response to Rous tumors in chickens.
the effect of major histocompatiblity complex haplotype on response to tumors.
the role of major histocompatability genes in tumor rejection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

B26 is the least effective B locus haplotype in the antitumor response to Rous tumors, B22 and B30 are more effective than B26, and the B locus haplotypes B26 and B22 complement each other in their antitumor response.
B22 is the major histocompatibility haplotype that confers the highest antitumor response.
B22 haplotypes have the most favorable antitumor response to Rous tumors, and B26 and B22 are the most beneficial haplotypes in tumor-bearing chickens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the B22 haplotypes are associated with increased antitumor response and increased survival.
the B22 haplotypic effect on tumor response was more important than the B26 or B30 haplotypic effects.
B22 is a dominant antitumor allele and B26 and B26 complement B22.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B22 haplotypes are the best responder to BH RSV.
the B22/B26 genotype has a significantly greater antitumor response compared with the B30/B30 genotype.
B22 haplotypes are associated with a better tumor response than other haplotypes.
